verdict.rationale: Unleash's activation strategies are documented to enable and disable features for certain users. The docs give the example of granting access to internal users alongside a percentage rollout, and Edge docs confirm targeting rules use user IDs and emails. Segments let these constraints be reused across flags. A hedged, dated community remark on limited targeting is not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the per-user allowlist/exclusion mechanism (e.g., userId constraint operators or IN/NOT_IN lists), explicit exclusion examples, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can target or exclude specific individual users for a flag (allowlists, beta testers, internal accounts)

citations.quote: They allow you to enable and disable features for certain users without having to redeploy your application.
to roll out a feature to 75% of users while granting access to internal users, you can add two activation strategies
user data (PII) used for targeting rules (like user IDs, emails, or IPs) is processed within the Edge node
A segment is a reusable collection of strategy constraints... you can define a segment once and reuse it across any number of feature flags
